Entries.Text: Finds the map textures that the selected map's map pieces and objects use but its map texture binders don't hold, and copies them in from the binders that do. Useful after bringing map pieces or objects over from another area.
Load a map and select it in the map list.
The map that is checked, and the texture binders its textures are added to. The binders are shared by every map of the area (one binder per map in Dark Souls II).
This map's area has no map texture binder in the project or game data, so there is nothing to add to.
Which parts of the map are checked.
Check only the selected map pieces and objects, instead of every one in the map.
Scan reads the models of the map's map pieces and objects and the names in every map texture binder. Unsaved map changes count: the parts are taken from the loaded map.
Find the textures the map uses that its binders don't hold.
No map pieces or objects to check.
These results are for {0}. Scan again for the selected map.
Textures are matched by name, as the game does. An object's own textures (in its objbnd) are used before the map's.
{0} textures used by {1} models: {2} in this map's binders, {3} in objects' own textures, {4} missing, {5} not found in any map binder.
Textures this map's binders don't hold that another map texture binder does. The source named by the texture's path is picked first; pick another where there are several.
Every map texture the parts use is in this map's binders.
Copy the checked textures into this map's binders. A texture's low detail version (name_l) is copied with it when the source has one.
Check every texture the filter shows.
Uncheck every texture the filter shows.
{0} binders hold this texture. The first is the one its path names.
Textures no map texture binder holds. Mostly expected: specular (_s) maps the game doesn't ship, lightmaps, system textures and placeholders. They can't be transferred.
Models or binders that couldn't be read. They are also in the log.
Couldn't read the file names of {0}.
Stop the scan or add. An add stopped part way leaves the added textures as unsaved changes in the Texture Editor.
Copy {0} textures into the binders of {1} ({2})? Each goes into the smallest binder, and the binders are written to the project at once. To undo, delete the added TPFs in the Texture Editor.
A target binder has unsaved Texture Editor changes. They are saved with it.
Copy the textures and write the binders.
Added {0} textures and {1} low detail versions, {2} binders written.
The Texture Editor's data isn't loaded yet. Try again in a moment.
